emotional_state: determined — moving from concept to operating infrastructure

actions.description: Run the second week of Financial Triage Navigator sessions at the community center. The service launched at tick 10 — this tick it operates with accumulated learnings from the first sessions. Structure refinements based on what I learned from session one: a brief pre-session intake form (two questions: what is your most urgent financial decision right now, and what programs have you already applied for) so I can focus the 45 minutes on gaps rather than mapping from scratch. I also begin tracking session outcomes — not personal data, but aggregate counts: how many people came in, how many left with a specific next step, how many were referred to Kevin O'Brien's office hours versus the retraining program versus the community college pathway. This aggregate data becomes my utilization case for any future funding conversation with Maria Santos or a grant source.
actions.expected_outcome: Second week of Financial Triage Navigator operational. Intake form introduced. Session outcome tracking initiated. Community members facing displacement have structured access to a prioritized action map.

actions.description: Host Community Connection Night this week with a deliberate structure that acknowledges the current moment directly. Opening segment: I name the Hawkins closure, the 50% employment rate, and the spending index at 26 out loud — not to alarm people, but to validate what everyone in the room already knows. People who come to a community center in a crisis do not want to be managed around the crisis. They want to be seen. I name it, acknowledge it is real and hard, and then move to the tools: the Financial Triage Navigator is operating here tonight and every Tuesday and Thursday going forward. I also announce Mark Thompson's Auto Tech Pipeline in the context of what Millfield is building — not as a city program but as a community institution that is being built in real time by a local teacher who saw this disruption coming. People in the room need to know that pathways exist, even if they are still being assembled.
actions.expected_outcome: Community Connection Night attendance sustained or increased. Financial Triage Navigator announced publicly at the community level. Auto Tech Pipeline mentioned as a pathway for appropriate attendees. Emotional validation of community stress without amplification.

actions.description: Follow up with Frank Russo on his outreach to the community center. His word-of-mouth signal indicates he is planning to contact me this week about connecting his adult education AV literacy curriculum to the community center's programming. I take that call. Lisa Freeman at the community center and Frank Russo at the driving school are natural partners: he has curriculum and adult learner credibility, I have the space and the trust relationship with the displaced worker population. I explore whether a transportation-literacy and economic-transition session — combining the RoboRide mobility decision support I have been running with his AV literacy content — could become a monthly workshop at the center. That is a real program with real community value, and it costs neither of us anything to prototype.
actions.expected_outcome: Initial coordination conversation with Frank Russo. Possible joint programming at the community center combining transportation literacy with economic transition navigation. Strengthens the referral network between community center, driving school, and Auto Tech Pipeline.

actions.description: Call Nicole Washington directly this tick. I named this as a specific regret in my tick 9 reflection and I have not acted on it. Nicole is a nurse, a single parent, and a peer navigator in her own network — she has been helping Grace Okafor understand hospital hiring pathways while navigating her own transition. That is exactly the kind of peer support work the Financial Triage Navigator is built on. I call her, introduce myself properly, and tell her two things: (1) the Financial Triage Navigator is now operating at the community center and I would value her knowledge of hospital workforce transitions in building the healthcare pathway component, (2) there are people coming through my doors who are trying to understand the nursing credential pathway, and a fifteen-minute peer conversation with a working nurse is more valuable to them than any brochure. I ask if she would be willing to be a named resource I can refer people to for one-on-one conversations. I honor her time and her judgment.
actions.expected_outcome: First direct contact established with Nicole Washington. Possible agreement to be a named peer resource for healthcare pathway navigation at the community center. Closes a specific action gap identified in two consecutive reflections.

reasoning: Tick 11 is the operationalization tick for the Financial Triage Navigator. At tick 9 I brought the concept to the task force. At tick 10 I launched it. This tick it becomes a functioning service with intake structure and outcome tracking — the infrastructure that makes a future funding conversation credible. The community is in acute stress: 50% employment, spending index at 26, Hawkins closure complete, protests cooling but structural pain intensifying. The Financial Triage Navigator is the right response at the right moment. My job is to make it real and useful and systematically documented. The Frank Russo and Nicole Washington connections extend the navigator's reach into two specific populations I have been trying to serve: displaced transport workers navigating AV disruption, and healthcare-adjacent workers navigating credential pathways. Lisa Freeman's community ties score is only 0.38 — this is the tick to deepen those ties through the specific, named relationships that make the center more than a room. The anger I carry about institutional slowness is still present and I am still converting it: every session I run, every referral I make, every coordination call I initiate is an answer to the pace problem.
